text.p: Japanese department store operator Takashimaya Co Ltd said on Monday a settlement had been reached in a lawsuit filed by shareholders over suspected payoffs to "sokaiya" corporate racketeers.
The company said nine executives, including former president Hiroshi Hidaka, will pay a total of 170 million yen in compensation to the company.

The scandal erupted last June when police arrested two senior officials of the company on suspicion of paying off sokaiya to ensure that its shareholders' meeting in May 1995 went smoothly. Hidaka resigned as president to take management responsibility.
Takashimaya said the agreement also stipulates that its shareholders' meetings will be open to the media from now on.
Sokaiya extort money from a company by threatening to disrupt shareholders' meetings or offering to prevent such disruptions. Japanese law has prohibited such payoffs since 1982.
Criminal charges have been lodged against the two former company executives who are currently on trial at Osaka District Court, Takashimaya said.
